title: Inferior frontal junction biases perception through neural synchrony.
abstract: How the primate attentional control network interacts with posterior sensory regions to bias perception is not fully understood. Using magnetoencephalography (MEG) supplemented by functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), a recent study reported that human inferior frontal junction (IFJ) could play a key role in biasing perception through neural synchrony with posterior sensory regions.
